bruce

Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator, generalised to any city.

bruce interpolates daily urban air temperature by fusing observation networks of different quality — official stations, airports, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen weather stations — with an optional gridded background (e.g. ERA5-Land). It was developed for Rio de Janeiro’s heat surveillance and is written so that any city with comparable data can use it: everything city-specific enters through a small data contract.

Model

For an observation of network k at station i, location s, day t:

η = β₀ + δₖ + x(s)ᵀβ + uᵢ + wₜ + ξ(s, t)

  • δₖ — offset of a biased network (estimated only for networks declared bias = TRUE)
  • x(s)ᵀβ — spatial covariates (elevation, urban fraction, …)
  • uᵢ — iid station effect (persistent siting bias)
  • wₜ — city-wide daily AR(1) term
  • ξ(s, t) — Matérn SPDE field with AR(1) dependence between days

Each network (and the background) has its own Gaussian likelihood with a fixed or PC-prior observation standard deviation. Windows (one month is the tested scale) are fitted independently with R-INLA.

Installation 

install.packages("INLA", repos = c(getOption("repos"),
                 INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep = TRUE)
remotes::install_github("asgouveiaa/bruce")

Data contract

object columns
obs station_id, date, value (one value per station and day)
stations station_id, source, and x/y (projected) or lon/lat
sources source, bias (FALSE = reference), obs_sd (fixed, or NA to estimate)
background (optional) date, value, x/y or lon/lat of cell centres
covariates a terra::SpatRaster, one named layer per covariate

At least one reference network is required.

Workflow 

library(bruce)
sim  <- bruce_simulate(seed = 1)          # or your own city's data

d    <- bruce_data(sim$obs, sim$stations, sim$sources, crs = sim$crs,
                   background = sim$background)
d    <- bruce_covariates(d, sim$covariates)
mesh <- bruce_mesh(d)
fit  <- bruce_fit(d, mesh, bruce_spec(), keep_config = TRUE)
bruce_check(fit)                          # every attempt, collapse diagnostics

pred <- bruce_predict(fit, n_samples = 200, keep_samples = TRUE)
expo <- bruce_zonal(pred, zones, id_col = "zone", weights = population)
cv   <- bruce_cv(d, mesh, scheme = "lso", checkpoint_dir = "cv_lso")

Degenerate fits

With clustered networks the day-to-day correlation of the field can drift to 1 and its variance explode. bruce_fit() checks every fit and, by default, restarts the mode search from a reset point and, if that also collapses, refits with the correlation fixed (fallback_group_rho, default 0.55). All attempts are kept in fit$attempts; fit$status records the outcome. See ?bruce_spec (on_collapse).

Status

Version 0.1: daily temperature, independent windows. Planned: sub-daily resolution, humidity and heat index, bivariate fields.

inst/examples/rio_adapter.R maps the original Rio de Janeiro inputs onto the contract.
